reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the two dates as two stages of one process — the surface looked dry on day one, but the muddy ground was not firm and walkable until two months later, marked even by a different Hebrew word.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells, who lists Genesis 8:13 and 8:14 as giving two different dates for when the earth dried after the flood.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "When did the earth dry after the flood?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/dry.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (print ed. 2013; online skepticsannotatedbible.com)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …a different word from that in the preceding verse is here used for "dry", this being a different kind, or, however, a greater degree of dryness than the other.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the two-dates tension by noting the Hebrew uses a different word in 8:14 than in 8:13, denoting a greater degree of dryness — the two verses describe distinct stages, not the same event on two dates.

excerpts.excerpt_text: He could see that the surface of the earth was dry; but it was not till the 27th day of the second month, 57 days, therefore, after the removal of the roof, that the earth was completely dried up.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly distinguishes the day-1 'surface was dry' from the day-27 'completely dried up,' framing the interval as the gap between a visibly dry surface and full drying — the harmonizing two-stages reading.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Though Noah saw the ground dry the first day of the first month, yet God would not suffer him to go out of the ark till the twenty-seventh day of the second month.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Treats the two dates as compatible: Noah saw dry ground on day 1 (8:13) but the ground was not yet a fit habitation until day 27 (8:14), so God delayed the exit — distinct conditions, not contradictory dates.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair directly, observing that 8:14 uses a different Hebrew word for 'dry' than 8:13, denoting a greater degree of dryness — so the two dates mark two stages, not a contradiction. Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this passage could not be confirmed.
